newsitem.title: FRANCE: ATHLETICS-DEJECTED PEREC SAYS MAY MISS WORLD CHAMPS.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-DEJECTED PEREC SAYS MAY MISS WORLD CHAMPS.

text.p: Dejected Marie-Jose Perec of France said she was considering missing the athletics world championships in August after suffering her second blow within a week on Sunday.

The 400 and 200 metres Olympic champion, who was a disappointing seventh over 200 metres last week in Paris, finished third over the same distance in Villeneuve d'Ascq behind Jamaican Juliet Cuthbert and Russia's Natalia Voronova.
"It's a little bit better than in Paris. But if in Lausanne it does not improve yet again, I'll put an end to my season. I won't go to the world championships," she said after clocking 22.67 seconds.
The Lausanne meeting takes place on Wednesday.
"I've won a world title twice already and if I don't feel well, I should leave my place to others. When I'm ready, I'll return," she added.
Algeria's Noureddine Morceli won the 2,000 metres but was made to fight by a mediocre opposition and finished seven seconds outside his world mark in 4:54.67.
Namibia's Frankie Fredericks was far more convincing, clocking 9.95 seconds to win the 100 metres ahead of Americans Tim Montgomery and Leroy Burrell.
American Bryan Bronson clocked a season's best of 47.77 seconds in the 400 metres hurdles.
Czech Daniela Bartova beat her own European pole vault record with a jump of 4.32 metres. The previous mark was 4.31.
